name: Arrow Rock (Melvern Lake)
note: USACE Melvern Lake park halfway along the south shore, on a point. 43 paved sites: 19 with 30-amp electric and water, 24 basic. Showers, flush and vault toilets, drinking water, a dump station, boat ramp and dock; the Tallgrass Heritage Trail starts here. Booked on recreation.gov for May 1-Sep 29. Generators are allowed on basic sites until 10 PM. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Bookable on recreation.gov for the May 1-Sep 29 season; 33 of the 43 sites are listed there and the rest are first-come. Stays are limited to 14 nights in any 30 days at the lake.
field_notes.Fees: recreation.gov 2026 peak season (May 1-Sep 29): $24 for 30-amp electric and water, $20 basic.
field_notes.Sites: 19 sites with 30-amp electric and water, 24 basic. recreation.gov lists 33 (all 19 electric plus 14 basic); the rest are not on it. Paved pads; sites 03 and 08 are long pull-throughs.

name: Banner Creek Reservoir (Jackson County)
note: Jackson County reservoir park on K-16 west of Holton, office at 10975 K-16 Hwy. Hook-up loops are Deer Run (A/B/C, same-day only, with the shower house), Cedar Point at the lake end of the north-west loops, the South Side peninsula loop, and the long-term Buffalo Run loop (by phone), which also has primitive sites. Pay daily permits at the courtesy box inside the gate. --Claude

Booking: min stay 4 nights on weekends, 7 on holidays

field_notes.Booking: Cedar Point and South Side book ahead on Campspot (4-night minimum on weekends, 7 on holidays); Deer Run is same-day only; the long-term Buffalo Run loop is booked by phone. Reservations open January 15.
field_notes.Fees: Camping with hookups $20 a night, without hookups $13 (tent/primitive and RV boondocking in Buffalo Run); $5 daily vehicle entrance permit (annual $45). Online bookings add a $6 Short Term Booking Fee once per stay. Pay daily permits at the courtesy box inside the gate.
field_notes.Sites: 86 hookup sites (the county adds 9 new ones in B section); Campspot sells 79 of them in six types, plus 15 primitive/dry-camp sites in Buffalo Run. Rigs to 40-90 ft.

name: Lake Afton Park (Sedgwick County)
note: Sedgwick County park, 720 acres around the 258-acre Lake Afton, W of Wichita. RV camping in several areas around the shore (Fisherman's Cove by the observatory, Shelter #5 on Fellowship Cove, Cottonwood Grove), with electric at many sites, water at 16 and restrooms (three open in winter). No generators. Permits at the park office or kiosk; 14 days, then 5 days away, 56 days a year at most. Blue-green algae warnings in summer (call 316-660-1780). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: No camping reservations: buy the camping permit at the park office or the self-pay kiosk ($5 more a day from park security). 14 consecutive days, then leave for 5 days (the rules) or 7 (the camping page); 56 days a year at most. Sites near the rentable shelters may be held for a shelter booking, so ask the office first.
field_notes.Fees: Sedgwick County camping permit, bought at the park office or self-pay kiosk: electric $17 a day ($104 a week), electric and water $19.50 ($119 a week; only 16 sites have water); primitive with no hookups $13 ($76 a week). Seniors 62+ and military pay $15 / $17.50 / $12. Add $5 a day if the permit is bought from park security.

name: Pratt County Veterans Memorial Lake
note: Pratt County's lake park: gravel pull-through service sites on open ground west of the lake road, plus primitive camping in designated areas and overnight camping on fishing piers 2-21 (not pier 1); fire rings, dump nearby. Swimming and wading are prohibited, and motorboats are allowed only for no-wake fishing. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Up to 14 consecutive days, then a 48-hour absence of people, equipment and vehicles before camping again. Holding a pier or service site with an unattended vehicle is prohibited.
field_notes.Fees: Pratt County: service sites 1-21 (water and electricity) $20 a night whether or not the services are used; primitive camping in designated areas and on fishing piers 2-21 $5 a night (no overnight camping on pier 1). A camping permit is required. Set by Resolution 3-6-2023, still the county's posted rule on 2026-11-06.

name: Atwood Lake (Lions Park)
note: City of Atwood lake park on the south side of Lake Atwood, run with the Lions Club: hook-up sites on a gravel lot by the lake's south-east arm, with showers. Pick up the permit and the hook-up key at the Atwood Liquor Store, 402 Grant on US-36. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Permit $25 a night for a hook-up site (weekly and monthly rates available), from the Atwood Liquor Store, 402 Grant on US-36, which also hands out the hook-up keys.

name: Sterling Lake (Sterling)
note: City of Sterling RV park on East Van Buren Street beside Sterling Lake: a gravel row of pads between the railroad and the park road, across the road and a treeline from the lake. Self-pay envelopes at the west RV entrance. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: RV spaces $25 a night year round (full hookups); tent camping $5. Self-pay envelope at the west RV entrance.

name: Washington City Park
note: City campground at 1100 D Street in Washington's City Park; pay at the campground drop box or City Hall. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: City of Washington: $15 a night, electric and water; pay at the campground drop box or City Hall. Page undated, live 2026-11-06.

name: Lone Star Lake Park (Douglas County)
note: Douglas County park around 185-acre Lone Star Lake, southwest of Lawrence, on the site of the 1930s CCC camp that built the dam (stone water tower and fireplaces remain). 62 campsites in wooded loops above the north shore, 19 with electricity; restrooms, swim beach, boat ramp, shelters and a rentable community building. Permits in person from the camp host, check or cash only; quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.; up to two shelters and eight people a site. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: No reservations: first come, first served, permit bought in person (check or cash). Fourteen continuous days, then five days away from the camping area. Camp host (785) 865-8466.
field_notes.Fees: Electric sites $16 a day, non-electric $11; permit required, check or cash only.

name: Winfield Fairgrounds
note: City of Winfield fairgrounds on US-160 at 1105 W. Ninth, by the Walnut River, open for camping year-round outside events too. Open camping areas with about 150 50-amp services on hard surface plus 20/30-amp outlets, limited seasonal water, a year-round dump station; the 44-acre Pecan Grove to the south has limited electric. Restrooms close in winter. After 14 days, move between the fairgrounds and the Pecan Grove. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: No site reservations: buy a 24-hour camping permit from the city (online ePermits link on the fairgrounds page) and take an open spot. After 14 consecutive days, move between the fairgrounds and the Pecan Grove.
field_notes.Fees: City of Winfield fee schedule (Jan 2026): all camping $17 per 24 hours; $5 primitive only under a special-event contract; groups of 75+ units $12 electric / $3 primitive. Each permit covers one 40 x 20 ft spot.
field_notes.Sites: Open camping areas, not numbered sites: each permit is one spot of at most 40 x 20 ft, and a bigger setup pays for a second spot.

name: Newman Park (Arkansas City)
note: City of Arkansas City park on W. Lincoln Ave: a small open camping area with no marked sites around a gravel loop with two covered picnic tables, plus drinking water and a dump station (11/2024 camper). On a 72-hour permit, 5 days at most (city fee schedule, January 2026). The city's pages don't say how to register. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: City fee schedule: 'Camping Permit Valid for 72 Hours (5 day maximum)'. The city's pages don't say where the permit is bought.
field_notes.Fees: City fee schedule effective January 1, 2026: $10 a day. A camping permit is valid for 72 hours.

name: 4 Aces RV Park (Kinsley)
note: Small private park at 1004 Massachusetts Ave on US-50 in Kinsley: level concrete full-hookup pull-throughs in an overnight section, with a separate extended-stay section. No office on site; book by phone and pay at the self-serve envelopes. Railroad close by. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $38-45 a night in August-October 2025 (RV Life reviews); the park has no web page (2026-11-05). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported: $38-45 a night for a full-hookup pull-through (RV Life reviews, August and October 2025); the park has no web page of its own.

name: Wolf Pond Park (Ellinwood)
note: City of Ellinwood's Wolf Pond & RV Park on the south side of US-56 (Santa Fe & Fritz), beside a small fishing pond and the grain elevator. Pay at the site or at the City Office, 104 East 2nd. Handy for Cheyenne Bottoms and Quivira. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Hook-up fee $8 a day, paid at the site or at the City Office, 104 East 2nd.

name: Steamboat Lake State Park (Dutch Hill)
note: Dutch Hill campground at Steamboat Lake: the Wheeler (electric) and Bridge Island loops. --Claude

field_notes.Season: CPW: summer camping from the Friday before Memorial Day (May 28 in 2027) to September 30; from October 1 to November 1 (2026) only Dutch Hill's Wheeler and Bridge Island loops stay open, booked on the day. Winter camping is in the marina parking lot (8 electric spots), not here.
field_notes.Booking: A reservation is required: cpwshop.com or 1-800-244-5613, up to six months ahead in summer. October 1 - November 1 (2026) sites can be booked only on the day of arrival. 14 days within a 28-day period; six people, two motorized vehicles and one camping unit per site. Check-in 1 p.m., check-out noon. Display a vehicle pass.
field_notes.Fees: June nights: basic $28; electric $36. The same on a Saturday. Plus tax and the daily vehicle pass. CPW's camping page puts basic sites at $22-28, electric $27-36 and full hookups $32-41 by park and season. Colorado Parks and Wildlife's booking site, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: Wheeler: 37 50-amp electric sites (116-155, one ADA), 20-45 ft, 36 of them 23 ft or more (site 136 is 20 ft), 10 pull-throughs. Bridge Island: 14 non-electric sites (166-180), 20-42 ft, 12 of them 23 ft or more (177 and 178 are 20 ft), plus 20 walk-in tent sites (181-200) where truck and pop-up campers may not use the parking. 48 sites take a 23-ft rig.

name: Moraine Park Campground
note: Rocky Mountain NP campground in Moraine Park, the Big Thompson River meadow below the high peaks. About 236 sites in five loops, 46 of them electric; rigs up to 40 ft, many sites tent- or van-sized and many not level. Flush toilets, dump station, solar shower stalls (bring your own bag). Reservation only in summer, first come first served in winter, when it is the park's only open campground. Rangers may enforce keeping RV windows closed due to bears. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Open year-round: summer reservation season (2026: May 21 to noon October 19), then winter first-come camping in Loops A (sites 1-62), B, C and E from October 19. The only RMNP campground open in winter.
field_notes.Booking: Summer season: reservation only on recreation.gov (no in-person booking), some sites up to 6 months ahead and some on short-term release; the reservation includes the Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road permit from 1 p.m. on arrival day. Winter season: first come, first served, paid by Scan & Pay or at an entrance station. Summer limit is 7 nights in total across all RMNP campgrounds.
field_notes.Fees: Standard non-electric sites $35 a night in the summer reservation season and $30 in the winter first-come season; electric sites $55 year-round. Senior or Access pass discount on camping, pass and photo ID shown at check-in. Park entrance fee extra.
field_notes.Sites: 236 bookable sites in the recreation.gov catalog (46 electric) plus 22 management sites. Vehicles over 40 ft, including tow vehicle and hitch, are not permitted; many sites are for tents or vans only, so check each site's length.

name: Ansel Watrous Campground
note: Canyon Lakes Ranger District, Arapaho-Roosevelt NF: in Ponderosa pines on the bank of the Cache la Poudre (a Wild and Scenic River) in Poudre Canyon, 24 mi from Fort Collins on Hwy 14. A 23-ft rig belongs in the upper loop; the lower loop's entrance has a hairpin switchback. --Claude

field_notes.Season: The upper loop is open year-round; the lower loop May 1 - Sept 20.
field_notes.Booking: Upper sites 2, 3, 6, 7 and walk-to sites 8-10 take reservations all year (recreation.gov shows them bookable Nov 2026 - Mar 2027); upper sites 1, 4, 5 and lower site 11 are first-come only, and the lower loop is reservable only in its May - September season. Book at least 4 days ahead; a reserved site must be occupied within 26 hours of its start or it is let first-come. Max 8 people per site.
field_notes.Fees: $29 a night in the peak season (2026: May 1 - Sept 19; 2027: Apr 30 - Sept 18), $20 off-peak and first-come. Fees drop 25% when the water is off. One vehicle included; extra vehicles $8 a night.
field_notes.Sites: Upper loop sites 1-7 (back-in, 36-40 ft; FS: spurs 25-45 ft) plus walk-to sites 8-10; lower loop sites 11-17 (back-in, 33 ft; 14 is tent-only). The lower loop is not for trailers over 20 ft (a hairpin switchback at its entrance); the FS page gives the lower loop a 30-ft overall limit. Sites 8, 9, 10 and 14 fit one vehicle only.

name: Sleeping Elephant Campground
note: Roosevelt NF (Canyon Lakes RD) campground beside Hwy 14 in Poudre Canyon, ~43 mi west of US 287, ~7,800 ft, in open ponderosa pine with a view of Sleeping Elephant Mountain. The Cache la Poudre River runs across the highway, mostly through private land here. Length conflict (2026-10-28): the campground page gives parking lengths of 15-30 ft and says this older facility will not take larger RVs, but the forest's campground-status table lists a 20-ft maximum spur. --Claude Online photos show at least a few sites that can take a class-B or small class-C, but reviews say the sites are short and unlevel: have a backup plan. --AWH 2026-10-28

field_notes.Fees: $23 a site; 25% off when the water is off. Max 8 people per site.
field_notes.Sites: Parking spurs 15 to 30 ft (the campground page); the forest's campground-status table lists the max spur as 20 ft. Rigs must fit on the spur. FS: 'an older facility and will not accommodate larger RVs.'

name: Bogan Flats Campground
note: Crystal River valley 1.5 miles before Marble (Aspen-Sopris RD, White River NF); widely spaced sites, several at the river's edge, paved campground roads. Concession-run (American Land & Leisure). The group campground is 1/4 mile east. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservable on recreation.gov; the 2026 fee season is May 13 - Oct 1 (no first-come season is listed). One family site is first-come. Booking closes 2 days before arrival. No minimum stay (recreation.gov's minimums are 0). 14 nights at most, and 14 per month. Campers must occupy the site the first night.
field_notes.Fees: recreation.gov 2026 and 2027: $32 per family site; the group site $166. The Forest Service page (last updated June 2025) says $34 per night.
field_notes.Sites: Forest Service: '40-foot maximum RV length'. The recreation.gov catalog lists 35 family sites (34 reservable, 1 first-come) with max vehicle lengths of 20-80 ft and seven pull-throughs, plus a group site 1/4 mile east.

name: East Marvine Campground
note: Trailhead campground at 8,200 ft in a conifer-and-aspen grove at the East Marvine and Marvine trailheads into the Flat Tops Wilderness, 35 mi east of Meeker via Rio Blanco CR 8 and CR 12 (Blanco RD, White River NF). Corral sites for stock users sit outside the main campground; the creek is about 400 yards away. Cattle may graze in the area. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: The Forest Service lists the 7 family sites as non-reservable, and recreation.gov's 2027 table is a first-come season only (May 13 - Oct 31, 2027). The one exception seen: in the 2026 fall hunting season (Sept 29 - Nov 1) recreation.gov took bookings for site 1 and the three stock sites. A site must be occupied the first night.
field_notes.Fees: $24 per single site; the three stock sites with corrals are $30. Same in recreation.gov's 2027 table. One RV per single site; an extra vehicle is charged per night at the campground.
field_notes.Sites: 7 family sites (30-ft back-ins in the catalog) plus 3 pull-through stock sites with corrals, outside the main campground and for stock users only. The trailhead parking areas have plenty of room for trailers.

name: Willows Campground
note: On the north arm of Green Mountain Reservoir at ~7,950 ft, off Heeney Road (County Road 30) just west of CO-9, between Silverthorne and Kremmling. Sites line the shore along a dirt loop; the reservoir is drawn down through late summer. Recreation.gov: site access is difficult when the road is wet. Motorboats launch only from Heeney Marina after an Aquatic Nuisance Species inspection. Length (2026-10-28): the forest's 2026 table gives a 20-ft maximum site, but recreation.gov's catalog shows roadside pull-outs of 30-93 ft. Have a backup plan. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Estimated dates; opening can shift with weather.
field_notes.Booking: All 21 sites reservable on recreation.gov up to 2 days ahead; a reserved site is forfeited if not occupied by 11 am the day after arrival. No day use. Check-in 2 pm, check-out 11 am.
field_notes.Sites: The forest's 2026 operating-dates table gives a 20-ft maximum site length; recreation.gov's catalog lists mostly parallel roadside pull-outs (catalog driveway lengths 30-93 ft) and one 25-ft pull-through (site 11).

name: Ute Campground
note: On a gentle south-facing slope under ponderosa pine just north of US-160, ~15 mi W of Pagosa Springs, facing Chimney Rock National Monument (summer guided tours; entrance 4 mi away on CO-151); gets very warm in summer. Hiking on Haystack Mountain. Length (2026-10-28): the Forest Service gives a 35-ft maximum RV and the site catalog lists 28-62-ft driveways, but a recreation.gov notice says the gravel spurs fit about a 20-ft extended-cab pickup. Have a backup plan. --Claude

field_notes.Season: May through September; recreation.gov has the exact dates (2026 season May 8 - Sep 26).
field_notes.Booking: Sites 08-12, 17, 21, 22 and the group site are reservable on recreation.gov; the rest are first come, first served. Stay limit 28 nights at first-come sites, 12 on reserved ones. Reservation season varies by year (May 8 - Sep 26 in 2026, Jun 5 - Sep 26 in 2027).
field_notes.Fees: $22 a single site, $100 the group site (Forest Service page and recreation.gov 2026-2028 rates).
field_notes.Sites: Recreation.gov lists 21 sites including one group site (the Forest Service page says 26). Forest Service: max RV 35 ft; everything with wheels must fit the parking spur, no overflow parking. Catalog driveways run 28-62 ft (vehicle maximums 30-40 ft where given), though a recreation.gov notice calls the gravel spurs about 20 ft.

name: Tom Bennett Campground
note: Small primitive campground near Pingree Park along the South Fork Cache la Poudre in lodgepole pine, elev ~9,000 ft; reached via well-maintained gravel Pingree Park Rd (CR 63E), passable by passenger cars. Length (2026-10-28): the campground page gives parking lengths of 15-25 ft and says this older facility will not take larger RVs; the forest's campground-status table lists a 20-ft maximum spur. At most a spur or two could take a 23-ft rig: have a backup plan. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Mid-May to mid-November (May 15 - Nov 15 in the forest's campground status table).
field_notes.Fees: Single site $19/night. (Forest Service page)
field_notes.Sites: Older facility that will not take larger RVs: parking spurs 15 to 25 ft (the forest's status table gives a 20-ft maximum spur). Vehicles must fit the spur; no parking off the road. Up to 8 people a site.

name: Dark Sky River Lodge
note: Former Rocky Top River Ranch, rebranded Dark Sky River Lodge under new ownership in 2024. On the Arkansas River at 10281 US-50 in Howard, ~12 mi from Salida; RV sites in three zones (Upper River shaded along the river, Lower River open, Lodge zone by the bathhouse and store). Also cabins, motel rooms and a seasonal bar and grill; bathhouse closed in winter. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Book online through the lodge's Guesty engine or call/text (719) 626-1429. Extended stays (30+ nights) by application and screening only.
field_notes.Fees: Base rates by zone: Lodge $39 (weekends from $45), Lower River $42 (weekends from $49), Upper River $45 (weekends from $55), before tax. Guesty quoted Upper River Site 4 at $45 + $2.44 tax for Tue 2027-06-15, no other fees. Extended stays from $650/month (30+ nights, screened).
field_notes.Sites: 13 nightly RV sites in three zones: Upper River (sites 1-4, shaded, closest to the river, rigs 25 ft or under), Lower River (6-9, open), Lodge (11-15, easy pull-in, for larger rigs). Back-in at least in the Upper zone.

name: Ute Bluff Lodge, Cabins & RV Park
note: Lodge, cabins and RV park on US-160 just east of South Fork, on the south side of the highway under the bluff, beside the Rio Grande National Forest; 30-amp back-in and 50-amp pull-through/back-in sites. River access is across the highway, not riverside. Also lodge rooms and cabins, hot tub, rec room with kitchen, trail up the bluff. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Book online (SiteMinder direct-book page; 50% deposit, or pay in full for the non-refundable rate) or by phone. One-night minimum.
field_notes.Fees: Posted $40 (30-amp back-in) and $50 (50-amp pull-through or back-in); the booking engine's Standard Rate is $42.80 and $53.50 with tax, the same for October 2026 and June 2027 (5% less non-refundable). Weekly 10% off; monthly $750 (30 amp) / $795 (50 amp). Pets $20 per pet per night.

name: Valley Sunset RV Ranch
note: Family-owned RV park just north of Hwy 92, ~1.25 mi east of US 50/92 junction in Delta (adjacent to Safeway). Directory listings describe ~66 full-hookup sites, 30/50 amp, ~25 pull-throughs, big-rig friendly (long sites 45+ ft), so a 23-ft rig fits easily; the operator's site gives no counts. Pool, hot tub, game room, dog playpen, playground, propane sold on site; takes both overnight/transient and monthly stays. Cabins and tent camping listed as closed (2025). Near the Gunnison/Uncompahgre confluence but not on the water (Confluence Park ~2 mi). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Lots: $38 a night plus tax; buy 6 nights, get the 7th free; monthly from $500 plus electric. Operator's rates page (Last-Modified 2025-07-26); cabins and tent camping listed as closed.

name: Wolford Campground
note: Colorado River District campground and marina on Wolford Mountain Reservoir, 10 mi north of Kremmling on US-40. Four loops on a point in the reservoir: A-C electric, D non-electric; sites are not level, so bring levelers. Winter camping in Loop A only. Boat ramp, marina, swim beach. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends, 3 on holidays

field_notes.Season: Dec 1-Apr 30 first-come only (cash or check), electric but no water or dump, minimal road maintenance; Oct 1-May 15 camping limited to Loop A.
field_notes.Booking: Book online (Firefly, the site's 'Book Now') May 1 to November 30; drop-ins welcome when sites are free, and December 1 to April 30 is first-come only. $10 to cancel; one night charged within 2 days of arrival.
field_notes.Fees: Electric loops A-C $40 a night ($240 a week); non-electric loop D $35 (tents $30). One camping unit, one vehicle and one boat included; extra vehicle $10, extra tent $20.
field_notes.Sites: 75 campsites in four loops (A-C electric, D non-electric) plus group areas. The engine lists Loop A sites for RVs up to 32-50 ft. Sites are not level; leveling equipment required.
